title: Unit-normalized derived comparison of K-injective mapping-fibre triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with ordinary unbounded derived categories $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex in $\mathcal A$ admits a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic chain maps from acyclic complexes. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], preserving K-injective complexes. Fix its total right derived functor $\mathcal G=RG$ and universal unit $\eta_K:Q_{\mathcal B}(GK)\to\mathcal G(Q_{\mathcal A}K)$, invertible on K-injective $K$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Then there is a unique natural shift isomorphism
$$\sigma_Z:\mathcal G(Z[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal G Z)[1]$$
with $\sigma_{QK}\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]$ for every complex $K$, using the canonical localization and termwise shift identifications. On K-injectives and their shifts it is induced by $G(K[1])\cong(GK)[1]$ under the unit identifications.
Let $P,P'$ be K-injective complexes of $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, let $u:P\to P$ and $u':P'\to P'$ be chain endomorphisms, and let $c:G(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ be a chain isomorphism with $cG(u)=u'c$. Set $H=\operatorname{Cone}(u)[-1]$ and $H'=\operatorname{Cone}(u')[-1]$, in coordinates $H^r=P^{r-1}\oplus P^r$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-ux,dx)$, and similarly for $H'$. Both $H,H'$ and $G(H)$ are K-injective. There is a natural chain isomorphism $\theta:G(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}H'$ with coordinates $(y,x)\mapsto(cy,cx)$ after the canonical biproduct comparison. Let $r:H\to P$, $b:P\to H[1]$ have coordinates $r(y,x)=x$ and $b(z)=(z,0)$, and similarly $r',b'$. They form the rotated distinguished cone triangles, with
$$cG(r)=r'\theta,\qquad\theta[1]G(b)=b'c$$
after termwise shift identification. Put $\bar c=Q_{\mathcal B}(c)\eta_P^{-1}$ and $\Theta=Q_{\mathcal B}(\theta)\eta_H^{-1}$. With the canonical $Q$-shift identifications understood, these give a morphism of distinguished triangles from $\mathcal G$ of the localized triangle $(H,P,P;r,u,b)$ to the localized triangle $(H',P',P';r',u',b')$, whose connecting square is exactly
$$\Theta[1]\,\sigma_{QH}\,\mathcal G(Qb)=Q(b')\bar c.$$
The comparisons are natural for commuting chain maps of the endomorphism diagrams; no exactness of $G$ is assumed.

proof.text: Regard the given universal-property bijections for eta as the assertion that (RG, eta) is a left Kan extension along Q_A (the usual universal-unit convention for a right derived functor). Precomposition by the complex shift, followed by the Q_A shift isomorphism, makes S_A composed with RG a left Kan extension of T_A composed with G composed with Q_B along Q_A. Postcomposition by the derived shift equivalence makes RG composed with S_B a left Kan extension of G composed with Q_B composed with S_B. The termwise and Q_B shift comparisons give an isomorphism of these source functors. Uniqueness of left Kan extensions gives sigma, and the factorization identity gives exactly the unit-normalization equation at every complex. The hom-ext identity for the first Kan extension gives uniqueness of sigma. These are Functor.isLeftKanExtension_iff_precomp, isLeftKanExtension_iff_postcomp₁, LeftExtension.postcompose₂, leftKanExtensionUniqueOfIso, descOfIsLeftKanExtension_fac and hom_ext_of_isLeftKanExtension in Mathlib. No choices of K-injective representatives or Hom lifts are needed.

proof.text: K-injective complexes are precisely the right orthogonal to acyclic complexes in the homotopy category (CochainComplex.isKInjective_iff_rightOrthogonal). That right orthogonal is triangulated; its ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₃ applied to the distinguished mapping-cone triangle shows Cone(u) K-injective. The shift instance gives H = Cone(u)[-1] K-injective. Repeat for u prime; hG gives G(H) K-injective. This is the homological-functor argument of Tag 090X.

proof.text: The canonical termwise cone comparison is Mathlib CochainComplex.mappingCone.mapTriangleIso. The cone map induced by c has inverse the cone map induced by c inverse; mappingCone.map_comp and map_id verify the inverse identities. Inverse rotation preserves isomorphisms and has the canonical natural comparison mapTriangleInvRotateIso. Their composite is exactly the already defined kInjectiveFiberChainComparison. Its second and third components simplify to c.hom. Applying the Q inverse-rotation isomorphism to the distinguished cone triangle proves both localized fibre triangles distinguished.

proof.text: Construct a triangle morphism t from Q_B of the termwise G-image fibre triangle to the specified RG-image triangle, with components eta_H, eta_P, eta_P. The first two squares are eta.naturality at the fibre projection and u. For the connecting square, expand the Q and termwise shift identifications, use the given normalization at H to replace Q_B(G-shift) followed by Q_B-shift and eta_H[1] by eta_(H[1]) followed by RG(Q_A-shift) and sigma, and then use eta.naturality at the connecting map P to H[1]. All three components of t are invertible by the given h_eta and step 2. Compose t inverse with Q_B of the canonical chain comparison. Its components are exactly the three displayed inverse-unit formulas; its third triangle-morphism law is the displayed connecting square. Transport distinguishedness from the prime fibre triangle through this isomorphism.

proof.text: Naturality of the termwise cone comparison is checked in each degree, precomposing by its inverse and using the two cone inclusions. The inl and inr equations reduce to functoriality and the diagonal cone-map equations. Combine this with mappingCone.map_comp and c.hom composed with a prime = G(a) composed with d.hom to get the cone-triangle square. Naturality of mapTriangleInvRotateIso then gives the fibre-triangle square; project its first component. For any chain map f between computing K-injectives, cancel eta at its source in eta.naturality to obtain RG(Q_A f) composed with eta_target inverse = eta_source inverse composed with Q_B(G f). Apply this to the fibre map and to a, then apply Q_B to the chain square and to the assumed c/a/d square. These give the remaining two naturality equations.
